findings.title: Optimized paginator crashes on datetime audit-log keys
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (paginator.py:840) runs math.floor/math.ceil on the order-by attribute, and value_from_cursor (paginator.py:843) returns the raw cursor integer. OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint wires this class in with order_by="-datetime" (organization_auditlogs.py:79-80). AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so any optimized_pagination request that returns at least one row raises TypeError inside build_cursor when it calls get_item_key, and the client gets a 500. A later request that supplies a numeric cursor also fails in build_queryset, which compares the timestamp column to an integer instead of converting the cursor the way DateTimePaginator does (milliseconds to a timezone-aware datetime). The new path is unusable for real audit logs; it needs DateTimePaginator's key conversion, not Paginator's numeric key logic.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets raise ValueError, they do not paginate
findings.body: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result slices the queryset with a negative start (paginator.py:880-882). The audit-log endpoint always passes enable_advanced_features=True. Django's QuerySet.__getitem__ does not support negative indexes and raises ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported"); it does not compile SQL or clamp the range. Cursor.from_string accepts a negative offset (for example "0:-5:0"), and that value is client-controlled, so an optimized_pagination request with such a cursor returns HTTP 500. The fallback branch (paginator.py:884-886) does the same for previous-page cursors. The comments that this reaches rows past normal pagination bounds, and that queryset permissions make that safe, are false: the call fails before a query runs. Negative offsets should be rejected with BadPaginationError, not sliced.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently rewrites negative forward offsets for every list API
findings.body: The new start_offset logic is in BasePaginator.get_result, which Paginator and DateTimePaginator share, so it changes cursor pagination for every endpoint, not just audit logs. For a non-previous cursor, a negative offset is rewritten to 0 and the first page is returned. Previously queryset[negative:stop] raised ValueError. Cursors are not clamped in Cursor.from_string, so a client can send "0:-1:0". build_cursor still derives the next offset from the original negative cursor.offset (offset + limit when the sort key is unchanged), so Link headers can keep publishing a negative offset and a client can loop on the same first page. Previous-page cursors still pass the negative offset through and 500. This is not a performance fix and should be reverted or turned into an explicit BadPaginationError.

findings.title: No tests for the new paginator or the shared offset change
findings.body: The PR adds OptimizedCursorPaginator, switches OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint to it when optimized_pagination=true, and changes slicing in BasePaginator.get_result, but no tests were added or updated. A request against the audit-log endpoint with optimized_pagination=true and at least one AuditLogEntry would have failed on the datetime TypeError; a cursor with a negative offset would have failed on Django's ValueError; and existing paginator tests do not lock the new BasePaginator behavior for negative forward offsets. Without those tests the 500 on the new admin path and the silent first-page rewrite on every cursor API can merge unnoticed.
